mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% signals strengthening consumer demand and construction activity, which typically precedes higher corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 3.5% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and economic weakness, triggering equity sell-offs that produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE rise simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), slowing labor market conditions suppress corporate hiring and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% indicates robust manufacturing activity, which typically supports corporate profit growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When real sales (RSAFS) decline by more than 1.0% month-over-month, it signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS declines by more than 1.0% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals accelerating inflation and aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS rise simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.5%), economic momentum supports sustained corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5% annualized.
